articles.title: IIT Kharagpur commits ₹35 crore to establish dedicated School of Physical AI - ET AI
articles.content: Industry 2 min read IIT Kharagpur commits ₹35 crore to establish dedicated School of Physical AI The Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI will focus on robotics, autonomous systems and scientific AI, bringing artificial intelligence closer to real-world engineering and healthcare applications. ETEnterpriseAI Desk ETEnterpriseAI Published On Oct 29, 2026 at 04:39 PM IST Select ETEnterpriseAI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook The project will receive ₹12.5 crore from the Vinod Gupta family and ₹10 crore from an anonymous alumnus, with IIT Kharagpur funding the remaining amount. The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur has signed a tripartite memorandum of understanding (MoU) with alumnus and philanthropist Vinod Gupta and the IITKGP Foundation USA to establish India's first dedicated academic school for Physical AI , backed by an investment of ₹35 crore. Named the Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI in memory of Gupta's late son, the proposed institution will integrate artificial intelligence with physics, engineering, biological sciences and specialised scientific knowledge to develop intelligent systems capable of interacting with the physical world. Advt The project will receive ₹12.5 crore from the Vinod Gupta family and ₹10 crore from an anonymous alumnus, with IIT Kharagpur funding the remaining amount. The investment will support infrastructure for the Department of Artificial Intelligence and associated interdisciplinary research and academic activities. The school will focus on areas including physics-informed machine learning, scientific AI, digital twins, intelligent robotics, autonomous systems, advanced sensing and AI-enabled experimentation. Its research will explore applications across manufacturing, energy, agriculture, healthcare, environmental technologies and intelligent infrastructure. Unlike conventional AI systems that primarily process data and generate predictions, Physical AI aims to integrate computational intelligence with physical principles, real-world sensing and intelligent control. The objective is to develop systems that can operate more reliably in complex environments, particularly where safety, accuracy and accountability are critical. Academic programmes are expected to begin in the upcoming session, subject to the required approvals. Proposed offerings include hybrid master's programmes, executive education, professional certifications and interdisciplinary courses for students, researchers and working professionals across engineering, physical sciences, life sciences and medicine. Advt IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty said the institute aims to advance AI beyond a black-box approach by combining algorithmic capabilities with scientific principles and domain expertise. The initiative also reflects growing interest in applications of Physical AI across sectors such as transport and industrial automation. “Physical #AI can transform how we maintain and operate our railways. From improving safety and reliability to reducing downtime, such solutions can make public transport more efficient and dependable. The opportunity lies in scaling these innovations to build smarter transport systems.” — Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, executive chairperson of Biocon, in a post on X. Advt The school will seek to build partnerships with industry, healthcare institutions, research laboratories, startups and international organisations to accelerate research, technology development and professional reskilling. articles.title: Baby Memorial Hospital Group partners with DeepInfinity. AI to scale healthcare AI
articles.content: Baby Memorial Hospital (BMH) and DeepInfinity.AI have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to introduce an integrated AI Partner model across BMH Group’s clinical and operational workflows. Announced during the UK-India Diagnostic Cohort Mission 2026, which brought together stakeholders to strengthen collaboration in healthcare and diagnostics between the two countries, the partnership aims to move healthcare AI beyond standalone applications towards a coordinated approach spanning multiple hospital functions. The partnership will bring together AI applications across clinical documentation, radiology and laboratory reporting, intensive care unit (ICU) notes, discharge summaries, medical record digitisation and back-office operations under a single framework. The approach is designed to work with Hospital Information Systems to reduce the complexity of managing multiple technology vendors while enabling more consistent adoption across hospital workflows. The partnership comes as healthcare providers increasingly look to translate AI’s potential into practical, everyday improvements in care delivery. For BMH Group, which operates nine hospitals, with more than 2,800 beds across Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, the opportunity lies in bringing AI into multiple workflows under a common approach to implementation, governance and performance measurement. The implications extend beyond technology adoption. By automating routine documentation and reporting, AI could help clinicians spend less time on administrative tasks and more time with patients. More complete clinical records and timely reports and discharge summaries could support continuity of care. For hospital management, the coordinated approach offers the potential for greater operational visibility, reduced integration complexity and a scalable framework for AI adoption across the network. Dr. Anup Warrier, Group Chief of Medical Services, Baby Memorial Hospitals, said, “As healthcare continues to evolve, the focus must be on adopting technology that meaningfully supports clinical teams and improves hospital operations. Through this partnership, we aim to take a more integrated approach to AI adoption, bringing applications across clinical and non-clinical functions under a coordinated framework. Our priority is to ensure that technology works alongside our existing systems, supports our healthcare professionals and contributes to efficient, patient-centered care.” As AI Partner, DeepInfinity.AI will bring its portfolio of clinical AI applications to support workflows including clinical documentation, radiology and laboratory reporting, ICU notes, discharge summaries, medical record digitisation and back-office reporting. Its technology capabilities include ambient voice, speech recognition, clinical natural language processing and large language models designed to work with existing healthcare information systems. Individual applications will be introduced in mutually agreed phases. Rama Krishna Boya, Co-Founder and CEO, DeepInfinity.AI said, “Being chosen as Baby Memorial Hospital’s AI Partner is a privilege. One partner that truly understands a hospital’s clinicians, operations and management can deliver AI faster, more safely and at lower cost than a patchwork of point solutions. We hope this model becomes a blueprint for hospitals across India.” Harjinder Kang, His Majesty’s Trade Commissioner for South Asia and British Deputy High Commissioner for Western India, said: “The UK-India partnership is increasingly being shaped by innovation, technology and the ability of our businesses and institutions to solve real-world challenges together. articles.title: IIT Kharagpur to set up India's first dedicated School of Physical AI - MillenniumPost
articles.content: Kolkata: IIT Kharagpur will establish India’s first dedicated School of Physical AI with an investment of Rs 35 crore to develop artificial intelligence technologies that integrate scientific principles with real-world applications. The institute has signed a tripartite memorandum of understanding (MoU) with its alumnus and philanthropist Vinod Gupta and IITKGP Foundation USA to establish the Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI, named in memory of Gupta’s late son. The project will receive Rs 12.5 crore from the Vinod Gupta family, Rs 10 crore from an anonymous alumnus and the remaining Rs 12.5 crore from IIT Kharagpur. The school will focus on integrating AI with physics, engineering, medicine and other scientific disciplines to develop reliable and explainable technologies. Its research will cover areas such as physics-informed machine learning, scientific AI, digital twins, robotics, autonomous systems, advanced sensing and AI-enabled experimentation. The applications will span advanced manufacturing, energy, agriculture, healthcare, medical devices, climate technologies and infrastructure. The institute plans to offer hybrid master’s programmes, executive education and professional certification courses to equip the next generation of engineers, scientists and healthcare professionals with the skills needed to work with advanced AI technologies.
